plan.headline: Rank organizations by count of product events in October 2026 and show the top one, with context on the runners-up.

metrics.title: Most active organization
metrics.description: The organization with the highest number of product events (logins and feature uses) in the selected period, with its event count.

metrics.title: Top organizations by activity
metrics.description: The organizations ranked by number of product events in the selected period, limited to the top N, to show how close the leader is to the rest.

metrics.title: Leader's daily activity
metrics.description: Daily event count over the selected period for the most active organization, to show whether its lead comes from steady use or a spike.

assumptions.label: Period
assumptions.rationale: The question names October 2026; custom dates are inclusive calendar dates.

assumptions.label: Timezone
assumptions.rationale: Day and month boundaries depend on timezone; UTC is the neutral default since customers span regions.

assumptions.label: Exclude test orgs
assumptions.rationale: The data dictionary says QA, demo and load-test tenants should be excluded from business metrics.

assumptions.label: Exclude internal users
assumptions.rationale: Activity by our own staff (users.is_internal) is not customer product usage.

assumptions.label: Count logins
assumptions.rationale: Product activity could mean all events or only feature usage; logins are one per session and are included by default as activity.

assumptions.label: Organizations shown
assumptions.rationale: Number of top organizations displayed in the ranking so the leader can be compared with others.

events.sql:
WITH filtered AS (
  SELECT e.org_id, count(*) AS events
  FROM northwind.events e
  JOIN northwind.users u ON u.id = e.user_id
  JOIN northwind.organizations o ON o.id = e.org_id
  WHERE e.occurred_at >= (:date_range_start::date)::timestamp at time zone :timezone::text
    AND e.occurred_at < (:date_range_end::date)::timestamp at time zone :timezone::text
    AND (NOT :exclude_test_accounts::boolean OR o.is_test = false)
    AND (NOT :exclude_internal_users::boolean OR u.is_internal = false)
    AND (:count_logins::boolean OR e.type = 'feature_used')
  GROUP BY e.org_id
)
SELECT o.name || ' (#' || o.id || ')' AS label, f.events AS value
FROM filtered f
JOIN northwind.organizations o ON o.id = f.org_id
ORDER BY f.events DESC, o.id
LIMIT LEAST(:top_n::int, 20)
events.explanation: Counts events per organization in the period (timezone-adjusted, honoring test, internal-user and login toggles), then returns the top N orgs by count.

events.explanation: Counts events per organization in the period (timezone-aware, honoring test/internal/login filters) and returns the org with the highest count, ties broken by org id.

events.sql: WITH filtered AS (SELECT e.org_id, (e.occurred_at AT TIME ZONE :timezone::text)::date AS d FROM northwind.events e JOIN northwind.organizations o ON o.id = e.org_id JOIN northwind.users u ON u.id = e.user_id WHERE e.occurred_at >= (:date_range_start::date)::timestamp AT TIME ZONE :timezone::text AND e.occurred_at < (:date_range_end::date)::timestamp AT TIME ZONE :timezone::text AND (NOT :exclude_test_accounts::boolean OR o.is_test = false) AND (NOT :exclude_internal_users::boolean OR u.is_internal = false) AND (:count_logins::boolean OR e.type <> 'login')), leader AS (SELECT org_id FROM filtered GROUP BY org_id ORDER BY count(*) DESC, org_id ASC LIMIT 1), days AS (SELECT generate_series(:date_range_start::date, (:date_range_end::date - 1), interval '1 day')::date AS d), daily AS (SELECT f.d, count(*) AS n FROM filtered f JOIN leader l ON l.org_id = f.org_id GROUP BY f.d) SELECT days.d AS x, COALESCE(daily.n, 0) AS y FROM days LEFT JOIN daily ON daily.d = days.d ORDER BY x
events.explanation: Finds the org with the most filtered events in the period (ties broken by lowest id), then counts its events per day in the chosen timezone, filling zero-activity days.

review.summary: The leader's daily series is computed correctly, but October is only partly complete (data ends 2026-10-27), so Oct 28–31 would plot as zero days and look like a sudden drop; the rewrite stops the axis at the as-of date.

issues.message: The days CTE runs generate_series to :date_range_end - 1 (Oct 31), but :as_of is 2026-10-28, so Oct 28–31 plot as y=0 from COALESCE; cap the series at LEAST(:date_range_end, :as_of) - 1.
